Indigenous Health Assessment (Adult 15–54 Years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 7-day history of intermittent fever with night sweats, generalized myalgia, nausea, reduced oral intake, fatigue.  
  • Recent travel to rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago with trekking/cycling and possible river exposure. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact drug unknown).  
  • Chronic postural back pain (under physiotherapy).  
  • Long-standing screen-related headaches/migraines.  
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Father: fatal myocardial infarction at age 68.  
  • Other family history not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Ibuprofen – OTC, recommended dose; short-term for fever.  
  • Paracetamol – OTC, recommended dose; short-term for fever.  
- Immunisation status reviewed:
  • Patient states “up to date,” including Hepatitis B (occupational requirement as nurse). No further details provided.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • Moderate exercise a few times per week.  
  • Current reduced appetite due to nausea; usual dietary pattern not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Non-smoker.  
  • “Moderate” alcohol intake; quantity/frequency not specified.  
  • No illicit substance use recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:
  • No ear pain or hearing issues reported.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  • Taking paroxetine; underlying diagnosis not discussed.  
  • No mood review or self-harm assessment recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes:
  • No visual changes noted; headaches attributed to screen use.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Works as a nurse; no further social history recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not ordered at this consult.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.
- Other pathology:
  • Ordered: Thick and thin blood films for malaria.  
  • Ordered: Inflammatory markers and additional blood tests to identify infectious source (exact panels not specified).

Management Plan

- Patient to attend clinic in central London today (or local Emergency Department if more convenient) for physical examination.  
- Post-examination blood tests to include malaria screen (thick & thin films) and inflammatory markers; urgency to be determined by examining clinician.  
- Clinician to document assessment and test requests in consultation notes for patient to present on arrival.  
- Administrative staff to arrange same-day appointment; patient instructed to phone provided number after a few minutes.  
- Advised not to return to work until investigation complete and fever etiology clarified.  
- Continue symptomatic use of paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed.  
- Ongoing physiotherapy for chronic back pain; no change to current plan.  
- Safety-net advice: seek urgent care if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks

• Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, BMI/waist, full immunisation record, detailed alcohol intake (units), smoking pack-year history (though non-smoker), comprehensive mental health screen (PHQ-9/K10), sexual/reproductive history, cervical screening status, basic cardiovascular risk assessment (lipids, BP), urine dipstick, vision/hearing screening, oral examination.  
• Internal contradictions: Patient initially “no headaches” but later describes chronic headaches—conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor repetitions but clinically adequate detail.
